Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:11:1.hebrew: לישהייה - מאן דלא גריס ליה סבר דכמו כן אינו דומה נמחק בן שני ימים לנמחק בן שלשה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:11:1.english: "Let him delay it" - One who does not have this [passage] in his text holds that likewise, [writing] erased two days earlier is not similar to [writing] erased three days earlier.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:2:1.hebrew: וניחוש דלמא שדי דיותא אמקום עדים - פירשתי לעיל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:2:1.english: "But let us be concerned that perhaps he poured ink on the place of the witnesses" - I explained [this] above:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:6:1.hebrew: אי לעילאי מחיק - לפירוש ריב"ם שפירש כשנמחק שתי פעמים ניכר שאין כתוב עליו, השתא קשה: לישדי דיותא בין עדים לכתיבה ולמחוק ליה, והדר לכתוב "אנחנא סהדי" וכו', דהשתא לא מצי מחיק ליה, לפי שיהא נמחק שתי פעמים ויהא ניכר. אבל לפי' רבי ניחא, שאינו ניכר כיון שאין כתוב עליו כלום. ומיהו עדיפא מינה משני, דבלא דיותא מצי עביד בין סהדא לסהדא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 164a:6:1.english: "If [they write] above, he erases it" - According to the explanation of the Rivam, who explained that when [the parchment] is erased twice it is recognizable that nothing was written on it, now there is a difficulty: Let him spread ink-gall between the witnesses and the writing, and erase it, and then afterward write "We, the witnesses," etc. — for now [in the Gemara's scenario] he cannot erase it, because it would be erased twice and would be recognizable. But according to the explanation of the Rabbi, it is fine, since it is not recognizable when nothing at all is written on it. However, [the Gemara] answers something better than this: that even without ink-gall he can do [it] between one witness and the next.
